title: intent/1 — what an organisation intends to do next
pitch: intent/1 is a small JSON format for publishing what an organisation intends to do next — one document per repository, served at the publisher's own domain, merged across an estate — and this repository is its canonical, vendor-neutral home.

refusals.title: Expiry is derived, never accepted as input
refusals.body: Every item carries expires, and the checker refuses any value that is not exactly asserted plus the kind's window — a blocker lives 14 days, a bug or a decision 30, a task 90, an idea 180. A writer who could set their own expiry could keep a dead idea current forever; re-asserting an item is how it stays alive, because somebody looked and said it again.

refusals.title: Filed is not published
refusals.body: An item is private until a named human promotes it. The reference constructor has no visibility argument; a public or partner item with no promotion record is refused; a promotion whose by is not a person/ id is refused. Agents suggest; humans consent, and the consent is a wire fact rather than a policy.

refusals.title: The served copy is a projection, never the record
refusals.body: A publisher serves only its public items at /.well-known/intent.json. Partner is not an exception — a partner-tier item behind no gate is a public item with a misleading label — and the checker and the consumer refuse a non-public item at a public URL.

refusals.title: Unknown keys are refused unless x- prefixed
refusals.body: At the top level and inside an item. A key nobody validates is a field a reader will start acting on; an extension declares itself with an x- prefix so a reader knows it is one.

refusals.title: Unreachable is not absent
refusals.body: A consumer fetches over https only, with a timeout and a size cap, follows redirects only within the same publisher, and never reads a network failure as 'they publish nothing' — that would be a claim about somebody else's organisation made on the strength of your own outage.

faq.a: A value for expires that is not exactly asserted plus the kind's window; a public or partner item with no named-human promotion; a promotion whose by is not a person/ id; unknown keys that are not x- prefixed; and a non-public item served at the public URL. It refuses and names the refusal; it does not guess.

faq.q: Where does this sit in Web 4?
faq.a: The discovery layer — the question 'who can accomplish this intent?'. A publisher states what it wants next and a reader, human or agent, finds who can serve it. The stack page and the Web 4 hub show where it sits among the nine layers.
